$comment: Hanse 508 geometry for sail-learn-and-train. Single source of truth for the 3D model and the rig solver. Units: metres and degrees. See docs/BOAT_REFERENCE.md for how every number was obtained and how confident we are.

meta.variant: Reference boat: in-mast furling main (manual, Selden, two-line furling drive), self-tacking jib on a Selden Furlex 404S manual furler, German mainsheet, rigid vang (Selden Rodkicker), single forestay, no gennaker rigged

frame.origin: Mast station (centre of mast section), on the waterline, on the centreline
frame.y: up is positive (y = 0 is the waterline)
frame.handedness: right-handed, matches three.js (x forward, y up, z starboard)

sourceKeys.brochure: Hanse 508 price list / spec sheet H508.22_PL_EN_20221216 (not stored in repo, copyrighted). Official figures.
sourceKeys.drawing: Measured from the brochure side view and deck plan drawings at ~35 px/m (side) and ~107 px/m (plan). Typical error +/-0.15 m.
sourceKeys.photo: Photos taken on the reference boat, stored in docs/reference/photos/.
sourceKeys.owner: Observed on board by the owner (stated directly).
sourceKeys.assumption: Engineering guess. Plausible but unverified. Safe to tune.

deckEdgeHalfBeam.$comment: [x, half-beam] pairs traced from the deck plan outline, bow to stern. Max half-beam 2.375 = beam/2.

sheerHeight.$comment: [x, y] height of the deck edge above the waterline.

waterline.$comment: Hull meets the waterline from fwdX to aftX (difference = LWL 13.54). Plumb bow; the transom bottom sits just above the water.

canoeBody.$comment: Hull bottom (without keel). Deepest point and a smooth fair curve to the waterline ends is good enough.

keel.type: L-keel (cast iron fin with bulb extending aft)

rudder.topYNote: The hull bottom rises above the waterline aft of x = -7.34, so the rudder top meets the hull just above the waterline (as in the drawing).

aftPlatform.note: Teak aft deck over the fold-out bathing platform.

mast.airDraftNote: Brochure 'mast length above WL approx. 22.05 m' includes masthead fittings. Drawing measures the mast tube top at ~21.55.
mast.sectionSource: assumption (in-mast furling masts have a large section with a slot on the aft face)

spreaders.source: heights from drawing, span and sweep are assumptions

backstay.note: Drawn as a single backstay. Split or single on the reference boat: unknown.

boom.maxSwingSource: assumption (geometry check: boom would touch the cap shroud at ~83 deg)

pitch.$comment: Boom pitch in degrees, + = boom end up. Phase-1 teaching approximation, prototyped in Python to satisfy PT-07/PT-08 smoothly. Tune visually, keep the tests green.
pitch.gravityDropNote: The rigid vang's gas spring holds the boom up against its own weight, so with no wind the boom only droops slightly. The mainsheet can still pull it lower.

vang.type: Rigid vang: Selden Rodkicker (size 30) strut with a rope tackle. Pulls the boom down and its gas spring also supports it from below.
vang.render: Two telescoping tubes from the mast foot to the boom, with the tackle running alongside

toppingLift.source: photo (line from the boom end straight up the mast) + assumption (exit height)

mainsheet.source: photo (both clutch banks carry MAIN SHEET) + drawing (positions)
mainsheet.system: German mainsheet: one rope, boom blocks <-> two deck blocks on the coachroof aft end, both tails led aft to the cockpit, no traveller
mainsheet.partsPerSideSource: photo: three blocks on the boom, two rope parts down to each spring-mounted deck block (docs/reference/photos/mainsheet-german.jpg)

selfTackingTrack.source: drawing (position, width), photo (straight track right in front of the mast)
selfTackingTrack.shape: Straight athwartships track in plan view
selfTackingTrack.halfSpanNote: Drawing gives about 0.9 m each side; photos suggest it may be longer (up to about 1.2 m). Unconfirmed.

jibFurler.source: brochure (manual jib furler) + photo (Selden Furlex 404S) + drawing

mainFurlingGearbox.source: photo (Selden manual in-mast furling gearbox with winch-handle socket and IN/OUT arrow) + owner
mainFurlingGearbox.note: Two-line drive: one line furls (rolls the sail in), the other unfurls. Backup: turn the gearbox by hand with a winch handle at the mast. Exact height on the mast estimated.

main.areaNote: Simple triangle is ~5% smaller than the official area. Acceptable for teaching.
main.furl: Rolls into the mast. Unfurled fraction f moves the clew along the boom: clewDistance = f * footLength. Luff stays full height.

jib.type: Self-tacking jib on a manual furler
jib.clewTrimmedRefNote: Clew fully trimmed with the car at the starboard end of the track (wind from port). Mirror z for the other tack.
jib.furl: Rolls around the forestay. Unfurled fraction f: foot and leech shrink towards the luff; the clew moves forward along the foot direction.

sheet.minClewToCarNote: Sanity reference only. The app computes the true minimum from geometry at startup.
sheet.purchaseSource: photo: two rope parts between the clew and the car
sheet.route: car -> along the track -> turning block at the mast foot -> aft along the coachroof -> clutch 'Genoa sheet' (starboard bank)

gennaker.note: Exists as a brochure option (176.4 m2, own halyard and 2 sheets). Not rigged on the reference boat. Data slot reserved; implement in a later phase behind a settings toggle.

reacher.note: Option on a second forestay (87.4 m2, genoa tracks). Not on the reference boat as far as known.

cockpitHardware.source: drawing (positions), photo (labels, layout), owner (which bank is on which side)

winches.note: Standard: 2 x Lewmar 55 ST EVO (brochure). Photo: one winch per side next to the wheel, aft of the clutch bank.
Option XC5200 drawn on the deck plan. Not on the reference boat (photo shows one winch per side). Do not render.

clutchBanks.sideSource: owner (the main furling lines are on the right side)

clutches.label: Main furling
clutches.tailNote: Left of the two: rolls the main in (owner confirmed the right one unfurls)

clutches.label: Main furling
clutches.tailNote: Right of the two: rolls the main out (owner)

clutchBanks.sideSource: owner (the vang is on the left side)

jibRollClutch.label: JIB ROLL
jibRollClutch.source: photo: on the port side deck next to the sprayhood, the furling line runs forward along the stanchion bases to the bow (fore-aft position estimated)

engineControl.type: Single-lever throttle/gear control (Allpa) with start/stop/power panel and tachometer

helmInstruments.note: Photo of the starboard helm: magnetic compass, B&G multifunction display and B&G autopilot control next to the winch; rope tails stowed in a bin at the helm. Phase 2+.

mastBase.note: All halyards and control lines come down the mast and turn at a ring of Selden turning blocks at the mast foot, then run aft along the coachroof in covered channels, one group to each clutch bank. Photos: mast-base-turning-blocks*.jpg.

ropes.$comment: Every rope the model knows. 'path' lists fitting/point ids from the working end to the tail; the renderer draws straight segments between them, except the 'working' segment which can sag. Static ropes are drawn but not controllable in Phase 1.

list.working: tackle along the rigid vang strut, mast foot <-> boom
two parts along the top of the boom from the sail clew (at the mast slot) to a block on the boom, then forward to the mast
list.coupled: hauled together with the unfurl tail, against the furl tail

list.working: mast gearbox drum -> aft; two tails: one furls, the other unfurls
furler drum -> aft along the port side deck via stanchion-base fairleads

list.note: With in-mast furling the main halyard stays hoisted.
Parked. Belongs to the gennaker (not rigged).

controls.$comment: All rope controls are continuous 0..100 with a user-selectable step (1% or 5%). Convention: 0 = fully hauled in / furled, 100 = fully eased / unfurled.

visual.$comment: Teaching approximations for Phase 1. Not physics. Tune freely, keep them here.
